subject: Motion to table
query: what is a motion to table
title: What is a motion to table? How the House kills a measure fast
answer: A motion to table is a quick, no-debate vote that kills a measure in the House. If a majority votes to table, the proposal is effectively dead, the same as if it had been voted down. Republican leaders could use one against Rep. Thomas Massie's resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
body:
House Practice, the official guide to House procedure, says tabling is "equivalent to a final adverse disposition" of a measure, not a temporary pause as "tabling" can mean in everyday speech or in some other bodies. The motion "is not debatable," so members vote on it right away. It can be made after a proposition is called up but before debate begins, and it is no longer in order once the previous question or the yeas and nays have been ordered. A tabled matter generally returns only by unanimous consent or a suspension of the rules.

Because any member can force a privileged resolution, such as articles of impeachment, to the floor, the motion to table gives the House a way to dispose of one without voting on its substance. Motions to table or refer a privileged resolution are in order, according to the Congressional Research Service.

ABC News reported on Nov. 9, 2026, that GOP leaders could move to table Massie's impeachment resolution against Hegseth instead of voting on the eight articles. Tabling needs a simple majority, the same as passage, so the outcome turns on how many Republicans join Democrats.
in_the_news: House Republican leaders could move to table Rep. Thomas Massie's resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when it reaches the floor in November 2026.

faq.q: What does it mean when a bill is tabled?
faq.a: In the U.S. House, it means the bill or resolution has been killed. Tabling is treated as a final rejection.

faq.q: Is a motion to table debatable?
faq.a: No. The House votes on it without debate unless members agree to debate by unanimous consent.

faq.q: How many votes does a motion to table need?
faq.a: A simple majority of members voting.

faq.q: Can a tabled measure come back?
faq.a: Generally only by unanimous consent or a suspension of the rules, although a privileged matter can be offered again. A timely motion to reconsider the tabling vote is also in order.

faq.q: What is the difference between "table" and "postpone"?
faq.a: Postponing delays a vote to a later time; tabling in the House disposes of the measure for good.
